stories.headline: 10-YEAR YIELD PUSHES BACK ABOVE 5% AS HAWKISH FED REPRICING CONTINUES
stories.body: Two days after the FOMC's quarter-point hike to 3.75%-4.00%, the 10-year Treasury yield climbed roughly 6 bps to 5.01%, closing out a losing week for stocks even as the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 both ticked higher Friday.
stories.explain: Wednesday's initial move lower in long yields reflected skepticism that the hiking cycle would stick; today's reversal back above 5% shows that skepticism fading as the market digests Fed officials' signal that at least one more hike is likely before year-end. When investors raise their expected path of future short rates, the 10-year's pricing formula — expected average short rate plus term premium — pushes higher even without any new Fed action that day.

stories.headline: S&P 500, NASDAQ 100 EKE OUT GAINS BUT STILL POST WEEKLY LOSSES ON RATE JITTERS
stories.body: The S&P 500 rose 0.17% to 7,650 and the Nasdaq 100 climbed 0.67% to 29,644 on Friday, but both indexes still finished the week lower as the 10-year yield's return to 5% kept pressure on valuations.
stories.explain: A single day's bounce doesn't undo a week's worth of discount-rate math: when the rate used to value future corporate cash flows rises, present values of those cash flows fall, hitting long-duration growth stocks hardest. Friday's modest gain reflects some dip-buying and short-covering, but the weekly net loss shows the market still repricing for a Fed that means what it said about more hikes.

stories.headline: WTI FALLS THIRD STRAIGHT SESSION TO $100 AS SAUDI PIPELINE FEARS EASE
stories.body: WTI crude dropped 1.6% to roughly $100 a barrel while Brent slipped 0.9% to about $103.87, with both benchmarks finishing the week essentially flat as traders concluded Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline outage will dent supply less than first feared.
stories.explain: WTI and Brent are priced off different supply pools — WTI off U.S. domestic inventories and pipeline flows, Brent off seaborne international cargoes more exposed to Middle East disruptions. The narrowing spread here reflects the market unwinding its initial fear premium: if the pipeline outage reroutes rather than removes barrels from the global market, the risk discount priced into Brent has less reason to persist.

stories.headline: GOLD HITS WEEKLY HIGH NEAR $4,400 AS FALLING OIL COOLS INFLATION EXPECTATIONS
stories.body: Gold rallied about 1.1% to roughly $4,391 an ounce, touching a weekly high near $4,440 intraday, even as nominal Treasury yields ticked higher — a sign investors read this week's oil pullback as taking pressure off the inflation outlook.
stories.explain: Gold is priced off real (inflation-adjusted) yields, not nominal ones, so nominal yields and gold can move in the same direction when inflation expectations fall faster than nominal rates rise. A third straight down session for crude lowers near-term breakeven inflation pricing (the gap between nominal and TIPS yields), which can pull real yields down or flat even while the nominal 10-year pushes back above 5% on Fed-hike repricing.

stories.headline: DOLLAR INDEX HOLDS FLAT NEAR 100.21 AS TRADERS AWAIT NEXT INFLATION PRINT
stories.body: The DXY was essentially unchanged at 100.21, down 0.02%, consolidating just above the psychological 100 level as this week's hawkish Fed hike is already largely priced in.
stories.explain: A currency's level reflects the market's expected interest-rate differential against other major economies over the relevant horizon, not just the most recent policy headline, so a flat DXY here means Wednesday's hike surprise has already been absorbed into forward pricing. Next week's core PCE print is the next real catalyst: a hot number would reinforce the case for another hike and likely push the dollar higher, while a soft one could undercut it.

stories.headline: SENATE ADVANCES PROTECT COLLEGE SPORTS ACT 74-24 AS NCAA ELIGIBILITY CHAOS PERSISTS
stories.body: The Senate voted 74-24 to advance the bipartisan Protect College Sports Act, an NCAA-backed bill setting federal guardrails on NIL spending and legal exposure, the same week a federal judge certified a nationwide class of Division I athletes barred from a fifth season and issued a preliminary injunction letting them keep playing pending the case. The bill still needs final Senate passage and House approval.

stories.headline: DOJ CRIMINAL PROBE DEEPENS CLIPPERS' KAWHI LEONARD SAGA WEEKS AFTER RECORD LEAGUE PENALTY
stories.body: Federal prosecutors in the Eastern District of New York are now criminally investigating the same endorsement arrangement that cost the Clippers five first-round picks, a $30 million fine, and a one-year league-wide ban for owner Steve Ballmer when the NBA handed down its penalties on Sept. 2 — the harshest salary-cap discipline in league history.

stories.headline: JOSH ALLEN ACCOUNTS FOR 5 TDS AS BILLS CHRISTEN NEW $2.1B STADIUM WITH 41-31 WIN OVER LIONS
stories.body: Allen threw three touchdown passes and ran for two more Thursday night as Buffalo routed Detroit 41-31 in the first regular-season game at the new Highmark Stadium; Bills receiver DJ Moore suffered an AC joint sprain and is questionable for Week 3 against the Chargers.

stories.headline: NO. 1 TEXAS HEADLINES LOADED WEEK 3 AS NO. 2 GEORGIA TRAVELS TO ARKANSAS
stories.body: Texas enters Week 3 ranked No. 1 in the AP Poll at 2-0. Saturday's marquee game sends No. 2 Georgia (2-0), a 24.5-point favorite after a 70-20 rout of Western Kentucky, to Arkansas (1-1, coming off a 49-14 loss at Utah) at noon ET on ABC.

deepDive.title: Why Oil, Gold, and the 10-Year Yield Can All Move at Once — and Not Contradict Each Other
content: Today's tape looks like it shouldn't add up: WTI fell for a third straight session to $100, gold rallied to a weekly high near $4,400, and the 10-year Treasury yield pushed back above 5%. If oil weakness signals cooling inflation, why didn't yields fall too? And if yields rose, why did gold — an asset that competes with real yields for investor dollars — rally at the same time? The answer is that these three markets are pricing three different things: nominal rate expectations, real rate expectations, and near-term inflation compensation, and they don't have to move together just because they're all reacting to the same day's headlines.

The transmission channel runs through breakeven inflation — the gap between a nominal Treasury yield and its inflation-protected (TIPS) counterpart, which the market treats as a real-time forecast of future CPI. Energy carries roughly a 7% weight in the CPI basket, and unlike most components, oil's pass-through to gas prices and transportation costs is fast, often showing up within a month. A third consecutive down session for crude gets read almost immediately as lower expected near-term inflation, which compresses breakevens even on a day when the nominal 10-year yield is rising for an entirely separate reason — in this case, the market catching up to Wednesday's hawkish Fed signal about further hikes.

What most people miss is that gold isn't priced off the nominal yield investors read in headlines — it's priced off the real yield, which is nominal yield minus breakeven inflation. If breakevens fall faster than nominal yields rise, real yields can hold flat or even decline, which is exactly the setup that lets gold rally through a day when the 10-year is grabbing headlines for crossing back above 5%. The 2014-2015 oil crash is the textbook version of this at scale: crude's roughly 50% collapse dragged breakeven inflation down for over a year, holding real yields low and helping gold hold up even as the Fed was preparing to lift off from zero.

The practical read for next week: core PCE is the data point that either confirms or unwinds today's setup. If the energy-driven disinflation signal shows up in the actual print, expect breakevens to keep compressing and gold to keep finding support even in a higher-nominal-yield environment. If PCE runs hot instead — meaning today's oil-driven optimism was premature — breakevens should snap back up, real yields should follow nominal yields higher, and gold's rally here would look like it got ahead of itself.
